neighbours.label: the first token of a new speaker's turn in back-and-forth dialogue: the opening quote and word of a reply line, or the colon after a speaker name in a transcript
fire:
"Did you lock the back door?" he asked.
"I think so."
"Well, could you check again?"

"The train leaves at six," said Mara.
"That early?"
"Yes, so pack tonight."

“Where were you last night?”
“At the library.”
“But it closes at eight.”

"Can I borrow your bike?"
"What happened to yours?"
"The chain broke on the hill."

HOST: So how did the band get started?
MILLER: We met in college.
HOST: And who wrote the first songs?

“You look tired,” she said.
“I didn’t sleep much.”
“No wonder, with that storm.”

INTERVIEWER: When did you move to Chicago?
DAVIS: Around 1985, I think.
INTERVIEWER: Why Chicago?
quiet:
"Did you lock the back door?" he asked.
She shrugged and went back to her book without answering.

"The train leaves at six," said Mara.
Tom groaned and set his alarm before going to bed.

“Where were you last night?”
He stared at the floor and said nothing for a long time.

"Can I borrow your bike?"
His sister tossed him the keys to the shed and left the room.
The host asked how the band got started, and Miller explained that they had met in college and written songs together.

“You look tired,” she said.
He rubbed his eyes and poured another cup of coffee.

"Is dinner ready?"
The kitchen smelled of garlic and the pot was still bubbling on the stove.
The interviewer asked Davis when he moved to Chicago, and he said it was around 1985.

notes: card/look: peaks are '"Yes', '"Well', '“What', '"But' opening a line that answers the previous quoted line, and ':' after 'GROSS'/'Steve Rush' in interview transcripts. Near misses keep the dialogue but start the next line with narration.
